title: Working with Types
summary: Compare core Python types and practice runtime inspection.

checkpoints.title: Built-in types
checkpoints.content: Python ships common types like int, float, str, and bool for everyday programs.
checkpoints.explanation: These built-ins cover most beginner workloads and are easy to inspect in the REPL.

hints.H0: Skim the sample describing each type in one sentence.
hints.H1: Look at the literal examples for each type.
hints.H2: Remember that every literal has an associated type.

checkpoints.title: Predict type() output

options.explanation: Floating-point literals use the float type.
`3.14` is parsed as a float literal.

checkpoints.explanation: Numbers with a decimal point default to the float type in Python.

hints.H0: Think about the presence of a decimal point.
hints.H1: Integers have no decimal; floats do.

checkpoints.title: Casting input
checkpoints.content: Convert a string input `raw_count` to an integer before adding 2.
checkpoints.explanation: Use `int()` to coerce the string to a number before arithmetic.

hints.H0: Find the built-in that converts text digits to numbers.
hints.H1: Wrap the variable with `int(...)` before doing math.
